title: Resource Multiplexing in Tuning and Serving Large Language Models
problem: LLM training (tuning) and inference (serving) have conflicting resource requirements and cannot efficiently share GPU resources simultaneously. Current systems either dedicate hardware to one workload or suffer significant performance degradation when sharing.
motivation: Efficient resource utilization for both training and inference is critical for reducing infrastructure costs in LLM deployment, where both workloads coexist in production systems.
method: Implements dynamic resource multiplexing that allows GPU memory, compute, and bandwidth to be time-shared or spatially partitioned between training and serving workloads. Uses scheduling policies to prioritize based on latency and throughput requirements. Likely employs kernel-level isolation or virtualization to prevent interference between workloads while maintaining efficient resource utilization across both phases.
key_novelty: Practical system for concurrent LLM tuning and serving on shared hardware with dynamic resource arbitration between conflicting performance goals.
contributions: Resource multiplexing architecture for concurrent LLM training and inference
Scheduling algorithm balancing latency-critical serving with throughput-optimized training
Experimental validation showing improved cluster efficiency and cost reduction
limitations: Limitations not discussed based on title-only analysis
primary_theme: Efficient resource sharing for LLM workloads
